summary: A short note from Postel and Kline pointing out that TENEX systems use link numbers outside the allowed range, which violates the official Host-Host protocol. This causes problems for some sites trying to connect, and the authors urge bringing TENEX into conformance.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 417 reports that TENEX systems used link numbers outside the Host-Host protocol's allowed range. The authors say this caused connection problems and ask the systems to conform.

questions: what was the tenex link usage violation
why did link numbers cause connection problems
what did rfc 417 ask tenex systems to do
subtitle: A warning about TENEX link numbers outside the protocol range

tldr.problem: TENEX systems were using link numbers outside the range allowed by the official Host-Host protocol.
tldr.mechanism: The notice says this usage caused problems when some sites tried to establish connections with TENEX systems.
tldr.outcome: The authors urge TENEX systems to conform to the established protocol.

today: RFC 417 is a notice about a Host-Host protocol conformance issue affecting TENEX systems. It asks for correction but does not describe the outcome.

sections.title: Link Numbers Outside the Allowed Range
sections.content: The authors say TENEX systems were using link numbers beyond the range permitted by the official Host-Host protocol. The RFC does not list the valid range or the specific numbers that caused the problem.
sections.plainLanguage: TENEX systems were using connection numbers that the Host-Host protocol did not allow. This notice does not give the valid range.

sections.title: Connection Problems for Other Sites
sections.content: The out-of-range link usage caused problems for some sites when they attempted to establish connections with TENEX systems. The RFC describes the effect but gives no further technical details about the failures.
sections.plainLanguage: Some sites could not establish connections with TENEX systems because the link numbers did not follow the protocol.

sections.title: Request to Follow the Protocol
sections.content: Jonathan Postel and Chuck Kline urge that all TENEX systems be brought into conformance with the established Host-Host protocol. This short notice does not specify a correction procedure or report whether systems were changed.
sections.plainLanguage: The authors ask the people responsible for TENEX systems to make them follow the Host-Host protocol. The notice does not say what changes were made afterward.
